members.title: Kraków shooting suspect who killed six has died, say police in Poland
members.lead: Terrorism investigation was opened after a 24-year-old opened fire in a market square on the weekend A gunman suspected of killing six people in a popular market square in Kraków has died in hospital, Polish police said early on Monday. The suspect, a 24-year-old named in local media as Michal O who authorities say was probably inspired by far-right ideologies, had been wounded in a shootout with police and had been in critical condition in hospital. members.lead: The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has said some progress had been made on what the “security infrastructure” of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia. Rubio’s comments on Sunday come as Russia-Ukraine negotiations under US mediation have been set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, with the talks expected to focus on postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and steps to end the war. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump’s son-in-law, will represent the US during the talks. The Kremlin insisted this morning that no European officials will be there, rebuffing France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noel Barrot, who said French representatives would ‌be present.
